newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government to meet opposition on TV package.
newsitem.headline: Italy government to meet opposition on TV package.

text.p: Italy's ruling centre-left coalition said on Monday it would meet the opposition Freedom Alliance at 1500 GMT to try to reach a deal on a jumbo package of measures for the broadcasting sector.

Fabio Mussi, leader of the Democratic Left group in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), said Post and Communications Minister Antonio Maccanico would meet the centre-right Freedom Alliance, led by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, "to see whether the final conditions exist for an agreement".
Parties in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government met earlier to discuss a proposed umbrella amendment to unify three decrees for the broadcasting sector that are due to expire soon.
The decrees include an extension of broadcasters' licences until January, a measure which mainly concerns the three Mediaset television stations controlled by Berlusconi.

Parliamentary sources said the government would tell the Freedom Alliance it was ready to extend the licences until May 31, 1997, with a possible further two-month extension, provided a government bill to reform the television and telecoms sector was passed by at least one house of parliament in the interim.
The bill's passage has been held up by filibustering and disagreement over a section concerning the creation of a watchdog for the telecoms sector after privatisation.
"There's a strong commitment from the government to approve a reorganisation of the (broadcast) system by March, extension or no extension," Mussi told reporters.

But he said any extension of the current ownership rules "must not allow the reform of the television system to slip indefinitely", adding the government was prepared to call a confidence vote on the issue.
"If a confidence vote is needed, it will be used," he said.
The government said last week an umbrella amendment to unify three broadcasting decrees should be approved by Christmas.
The planned package also contains measures to safeguard state broadcaster RAI and limits on the powers of a parliamentary watchdog commission for the broadcast sector.
The three decrees rolled into the jumbo package were all due to expire before Christmas.
The Constitutional Court ruled two years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels and set August 1996 as the deadline for changes to be implemented.

The government extended the current rules until the end of January 1997 after that deadline passed in order to plug a legal gap in which magistrates could technically have forced Berlusconi to take one of his channels off the air.
Post and Communications Undersecretary Vicenzo Vita told La Repubblica daily the government had made concessions over the package and the Freedom Alliance must "take it or leave it".
But he warned that if it went to a confidence vote, the government would present its own text, "not a compromise".
The package will be examined by the Culture and Transport and Communications Commissions of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Tuesday.
